title: Set a judge's threshold in the gap
statement: Set a judge's pass threshold in the gap between its lowest-scoring labelled pass and highest-scoring labelled miss, after checking the gap holds across repeated runs.
example: On 82 labelled cases the lowest passing mean was 0.61 and the highest failing mean 0.07, so the threshold went at 0.35.
detail: A reading course moved its closing-question judge to a vote-based model judge only where the new judge matched or beat the current one on labelled cases. With 7 votes per case it got all 82 labelled cases right, and that held on every one of 6 runs at 5, 7 and 10 votes; the lowest passing mean was 0.61, the highest failing mean 0.07, and the threshold of 0.35 sits roughly in the middle of that gap, with 0 false passes and 0 false misses. On 27 trap cases the gap ran from 0.85 down to 0.05 over 5 runs. Where the same judge got 28 of 36 on a four-way classification, worse than the current judge, it was not adopted.
against: This is one judge on one course's closing questions, where the two classes sat far apart; the record says nothing about where to put the threshold when labelled passes and misses overlap.

evidence.quote: A judge moved to Jev only where it matched or beat the current judge on labelled cases.
**Jev.** 7 votes on a `noul` question against the node's own rubric and required criterion: **82/82 OK**. That held on every run: 6 runs at 5, 7 and 10 votes.
Lowest pass mean: 0.61. Highest miss mean: 0.07.
The threshold is **0.35**, roughly the middle of that gap.
Misses: 0 false passes and 0 false misses.
**Jev.** 7 and 10 votes: **27/27 OK** on 5 runs. Lowest pass mean: 0.85. Highest miss mean: 0.05.
Jev ran 7 votes on a `choice` question with 4 classes and got **28/36 (78%)** against the agent's labels.
**Verdict.** Worse than the current (human-read) judge. **Not adopted.**
